title: Reading notes — LLM inference optimizations (ICLR 2025 + recent papers)
content:
Quick brain dump from recent reading (ICLR 2025 sessions + arXiv papers + internal runtime thread). Mostly for my own reference and to seed experiments with runtime team. Clean up later for a shared doc.

Top-level takeaways:
- Continuous batching + prefix KV caching remains the best first-order win for throughput without huge latency regressions. Papers at ICLR emphasized smarter batch composition (latency-aware batching) over simply increasing batch sizes.
- FlashAttention-style kernel improvements + attention tiling give measurable p50/p95 improvements on A100/RTX-class GPUs, but p99 still often dominated by scheduling overheads and straggler requests. Need to measure p99 in our sim rig, not just p50.
- 4-bit/3-bit quantization (GPTQ-like + group-wise) looks promising for cost reduction, but several papers show non-uniform quality drop across tasks: summarization and code synthesis are sensitive. Recommendation: per-workload quant profile + eval suite before rollout.
- MoE and conditional compute can reduce FLOPs for sparse workloads, but introduces tail latency due to routing and load imbalance — interesting for batch-heavy throughput jobs, less for low-latency API.

Notes on specific papers / links: 
- "Latency-aware Batching for LLMs" (ICLR 2025 workshop) — key idea: assign soft deadlines to requests, form micro-batches with deadline-aware batching so high-priority short requests aren't held behind large long ones. Implementation note: requires token-level metadata and priority queues in router. Related to our smart routing feature.
- "Efficient KV-Cache Prefetching" (arXiv:2408.12345) — prefetch next KV blocks for streaming/long-context scenarios; big win for chat-style workloads when users generate many tokens in bursts. Will need adaptive prefetch heuristics to avoid wasted memory.
- "Quantization-aware scheduling" (paper + code) — if kernels differ by quant type (FP16 vs INT4), scheduler needs to coalesce same-type requests or accept halved throughput for mixed-quant batches. Could surface as model-variant routing policy in console.

ICLR talk notes (informal):
- Panel: "Serving at scale" — people argued for more co-design between compiler, kernel, and runtime. One org open-sourced a small scheduler that does dynamic kernel selection based on recent seq-length distribution — seems similar to our kernel-selection heuristics.
- Demo: real-time eval dashboards to detect quality regressions after quantized rollout. They had test harness + synthetic prompt bank (1000 prompts) that runs nightly + on-rollout. This is close to Redwood Optimize evals; consider adding a tiered smoke test for canaries.

Experiments to run (prio order):
1) Batch composition sweep: run workload trace (customer-sim) with our dynamic batching vs fixed-batch sizes. Measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Baseline: current hosted runtime config. (Owner: me + runtime infra).
2) Quantized model eval: INT8/4/3 profiles on summarization & code-gen sets. Use our evaluation harness (existing scripts) — record relative ROUGE/ExactMatch and latency delta. TODO: pick 3 customer prompt-sets to simulate.
3) Prefetch heuristic prototype: implement simple token-prefetch policy based on recent token rates and measure memory overhead vs hit-rate.
4) Mixed-model scheduling: simulate scheduler that groups by kernel type and compare latency tail for mixed traffic.

Operational notes / rough API ideas:
- Expose per-route "quality budget" (max acceptable quality delta vs baseline) and optimizer suggests quantization profile constrained by that budget. Useful for dedicated/private customers who want predictable SLAs.
- Add rollout gate: require nightly smoke eval + p99 latency test on canary capacity before full rollout.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to attach "priority" metadata from upstream customers? Should be part of our API (client sets priority=low/normal/high) or we derive heuristics from request patterns? (Slack thread: #runtime-priorities).
- Memory accounting for prefetching — can we evict cold KV entries safely? What's an eviction policy that minimizes cache miss cost?
- Need a better synthetic prompt bank that represents production distribution (mix of short queries, long chats, multi-turn). Who owns building that? (ping Marco).

Links referenced / bookmarks (raw):
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12345  (KV prefetch paper)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412  (scheduling prototype PR)
- CONFLUENCE-ENG/serving-runtime-kernel-selection  (internal notes)
- JIRA-INF-6789 (prefetch experiment task)

Meeting notes: planned sync with runtime team next Thu (2025-02-20) to align on experiment ownership. Agenda: batch-sweep plan, quant eval infra, prefetch prototype.

Quick checklist: 
- [ ] write up batch-sweep reproducible script + dataset (trace)
- [ ] add quant-eval to nightly harness
- [ ] prototype simple prefetch in dev branch (PR 412 follow-up)
- [ ] propose console UX for "quality budget"

Random scribbles: 
- p99 often > 3x p50 for chat workloads (need to quantify).
- consider per-customer model pinning during quant rollouts to avoid regressions.

End of notes for now. Will tidy and move to shared drive if useful for runtime folks. If Marco/Samira have edits, ask them to add comments or push to PR.
